candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'I swear unto you, that I understand this mystery. For I have read the tablets of heaven, and have seen the holy books, and have found written therein and inscribed regarding them: That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, and written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness' — the heavenly-tablets witness to the good destiny of the righteous dead. Tewahedo eschatology preserves the heavenly-tablets image as load-bearing in the doctrine that the righteous dead are NOT merely waiting passively — their joy is already INSCRIBED, prepared in advance.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, and their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One unto all the generations of the world' — the soul-lives-on-and-rejoices promise. Direct anticipation of Phil 1:23 ('to depart and to be with Christ') and Lk 23:43 ('to-day shalt thou be with me in paradise'). Tewahedo soteriology preserves the intermediate-state-as-joyful (not merely Sheol-as-shade) as canonical.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And know ye that into Sheol shall they bring your souls, and there shall they be in great tribulation. And into darkness and chains and a burning flame, where there is grievous judgement, shall your spirits enter' — the sinners' destiny as darkness-and-flame. Tewahedo eschatology preserves the dual-destiny structure (joy for righteous, darkness-and-flame for sinners) and notes the verbal continuity with Mt 8:12, 22:13, 25:30 ('outer darkness') and Mt 13:42 ('furnace of fire'). The Synoptic image is Enochic in vocabulary.
